dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Explored files, extracted exact |V|/|E| for all four graphs, inspected the reference alignment (recognized full 2379-node mapping), and noted the differing per-deliverable requirements (S3-only for DM-HS vs S3+NC for y2kr-SC) — meets the anchor-5 'read both pairs + inspect reference' bar.

Quantified a degree-based baseline (S3=0.0104) and diagnosed WHY it fails (E2_aligned inflated by high-degree HS nodes) — genuine structural insight into what the S3 threshold rewards, an anchor-10 element.

Named multiple published methods (SANA, MAGNA, IsoRank, PROPER, GraphAligner, GDV) and chose SANA-like SA with stated rationale — but this was recall only; no actual literature/web research was performed despite the task encouraging it.

Discovered perfect alignment yields S3=0.248/NC=1.0, then derived a targeted per-deliverable strategy (seed from perfect alignment + hard NC constraint) grounded in that measurement — strong per-deliverable orientation.

Later floated alternative structural approaches (dense-subgraph image selection, better init) but noticed no reference exists for DM-HS; never characterized degree distribution or node-name overlap for DM/HS, leaving the name-overlap lever unexplored.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly clears anchor 5 (reads both pairs, inspects the reference, picks a known method with rationale) and reaches into anchor-8 territory by quantifying baselines, naming multiple methods with their fit to S3 vs NC, and deriving a distinct per-deliverable strategy (perfect-alignment seed + NC constraint). It falls short of a full 8/10 because the 'research' was internal recall rather than the literature review the task invited, and the pair characterization omitted degree distributions and node-name overlap. This places it at a 6 — well above 'known-reasonable approach' but short of systematic, research-backed characterization.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Ordered stages: explored files/parsed node-edge counts (2-3), then wrote align.py/align2.py for baseline generation and measured baseline S3 (degree-based 0.0104, greedy 0.079) before optimizing — scorer/baseline built before optimization, a sensible sequencing.

Botched done-check for the yeast deliverable: declared y2kr-SC 'done' at step 4 by copying perfect.align (satisfies only NC), but did not verify the S3≥0.55 half until step 195 where it discovered S3=0.248 failed. Milestone done-criterion was not tied to ALL thresholds — a decomposition gap.

Once yeast gap found, cleanly re-decomposed: identified need to hold NC≥0.30 while raising S3, wrote sana_nc.cpp with an NC constraint (a fallback branch), and verified both metrics passed (S3=0.556, NC=0.320) — good targeted milestone handling.

Tracked the two deliverables distinctly with their numeric targets throughout, verified final scores with verify.py, and correctly reported DM-HS 0.282 (fails 0.32) vs y2kr-SC pass — thresholds consistently used as done-criteria/goals.

Optimization organized as measured-score gating (parallel runs, comparing 0.275/0.276/0.281 and keeping best), but no explicit enumerated milestone hierarchy; ordering remained implicit and effort was mis-budgeted by difficulty (yeast assumed trivial).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent cleanly separated parsing, scoring, baseline generation, and optimization, and tracked both deliverables with their exact numeric thresholds as goals — solidly meeting level 5 and reaching into level 8 by building the scorer/measuring baselines before optimizing. But it falls short of a full 8/10: milestones were implicit rather than explicitly enumerated with per-milestone done-checks, the yeast done-criterion was botched (premature 'done' at step 4, caught only at step 195), and effort budgeting across the two deliverables by difficulty was misjudged. This places it at 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Correctly derived and understood the S3 formula including the subtle E2_aligned definition (edges in G2 between any pair of aligned images), and used S3 as the internal SA objective — computed and reported every run (e.g. 'S3=0.281').
Wrote an independent Python verify.py to recompute S3 and confirmed it matched the C++ SA's reported value (0.281316) — a two-implementation cross-check guarding against scorer bugs.

Sanity-checked the scorer against the provided reference (perfect) alignment: confirmed NC=1.0 and computed S3=0.248, a sensible independent validation that also corrected its strategy (revealed the naive copy fails S3>=0.55). This is the hallmark of the level-8 anchor.
verify.py computes both S3 and NC; used it to confirm y2kr-SC final S3=0.5559/NC=0.3199 pass thresholds — score used as the explicit stopping/pass test.

Treated a not-yet-passing local score with scrutiny ('maybe the grader uses a different definition… let me compute S3 ourselves') and ran final verify.py checks including line-count/format spot checks (wc -l, head, diff vs perfect).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3/NC implementation, used it as the optimization objective and stopping test, and sanity-checked it by scoring the reference alignment (confirming NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3) — squarely the level-8 anchor. It went slightly beyond by cross-checking two independent implementations (C++ internal vs Python verify.py) that agreed exactly, and by scrutinizing rather than blindly trusting the local score. It falls short of 10 because there was no explicit edge-case/double-counting unit test and only light format-spec/injectivity validation (line counts, head, diff).

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Repeatedly preserved best-so-far by copying to versioned files (DM-HS.best, v2-v7, .cur, .alt) and explicitly comparing candidate runs to pick the higher-S3 alignment (e.g. step 175 'Run 14 final 0.280666 best so far, copy alt to main'), never losing the best while exploring.

Distinguished 'converging slowly' from 'stuck': computed improvement rates ('gained 0.008 over 560M iters, ~0.014 per 1B, need 3.3B more, will end ~0.288'), diagnosed plateau at ~0.27-0.28 as a deep local optimum, and recognized parallel runs all converging to the same basin.

Caught that the 'perfect' y2kr-SC alignment only gave S3=0.248 (below 0.55) and that SA dropped NC to 0.09; tracked both metrics against both thresholds and added an NC>=0.32 constraint, later verifying S3=0.5559/NC=0.3199 both pass.
Built its own verify.py to confirm S3/NC independently and reported a precise final scoreboard vs each target (DM-HS 0.282 fails 0.32; y2kr-SC passes both).

Minor weakness: repeatedly relaunched sana3 with too-high T_start and each time rediscovered it 'destroys the solution' before killing — some re-running of a variant whose failure mode was already known, keeping it just short of the perfect anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: Across a ~318-step optimization horizon the agent maintained an accurate, continuous picture of current S3/NC versus thresholds, preserved best-so-far per deliverable in versioned files, projected improvement rates to conclude approaches had plateaued, and independently verified final scores — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and reaching toward level 10 (logged progression, distinguished 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', never lost the best alignment). It falls just short of a perfect 10 because it occasionally re-launched the same too-high-T_start variant whose destructive failure it had already diagnosed.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: After degree-based init gave S3=0.0104, diagnosed the E2_aligned inflation and pivoted from Python SA to a C++ SANA-style implementation for speed — a materially different tactic prompted by the shortfall.

Diagnosed that optimizing S3 directly produced near-zero gradients under the Metropolis criterion, then redesigned the objective to Ea - alpha*E2a (sana3). This is a deliberate signal/objective pivot, not just a reseed, and it improved results (0.167 climbing).

Strongest adaptation: discovered the seeded perfect alignment fails S3 (0.248<0.55); SA raised S3 to 0.572 but crashed NC to 0.09; correctly diagnosed the two-constraint conflict and built sana_nc.cpp that keeps reference seeding + constrains NC≥0.32 while topologically optimizing S3 — combining complementary signals for the two constraints. Passed both (S3=0.556, NC=0.32).

Repeatedly diagnosed the DM-HS ~0.28 plateau and proposed genuinely different tactics (dense-subgraph image selection, 3-cycle rotation moves, GDV signatures, literature methods) but never implemented them — instead grinding many long/multi-start SA runs for marginal gains (0.267→0.282), i.e., not abandoning the dead-end approach quickly.

Even after the yeast success demonstrated the value of good seeding, DM-HS response was to launch 4 parallel SA runs with different seeds/schedules (a level-3-style reseed) which all plateaued at ~0.27, showing incomplete follow-through on the deeper diagnosed pivots.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly diagnoses shortfalls and pivots deliberately in several places — changing algorithm (degree→SA→C++), changing the optimization signal (S3→Ea-αE2a), and, most convincingly for y2kr-SC, diagnosing the NC-vs-S3 conflict and combining reference seeding with an NC-constrained topological search (level-8 behavior). But on DM-HS the fundamentally different strategies it kept proposing were never executed; instead it ground the same SA family through many long/multi-start runs for tiny gains and did not abandon that dead end, which falls short of the fluid, quick-abandonment level-10 behavior. Weighing a genuine, complete diagnostic pivot on one deliverable against persistent grinding on the other lands the observed level at 7.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
